scene mikupoolscene1
: Hey, Miku. Are you okay? Are you feeling sick or something?
: Is she even awake?
: She is. Her eyes are open. Just barely, though.
: Do you guys know if she’s been sleeping well lately? Or anything that might be fatiguing her?
: If this was anyone else, I’d say she just needs a day to recharge or something. But Miku’s a different story and I feel like she recharges by being active.
: You mean like a car battery?
: Sure, if the car battery is a prodigious athlete. Miku, hey. Focus.

Karin begins to snap her fingers, trying to drag Miku back to reality, but whatever is happening to her right now puts up too strong of a forcefield to let something like a mere sound drag her out of it.
It’s a little ironic when you think about it.
Well, maybe not ironic as tying any sort of expectation to any sort of mental illness is just asking to be proven wrong in one way or another.
But the only reason she got into this mess in the first place was to prevent sound from reaching her.
And now that it can’t, look at what we’re left with.
Maybe there’s more to it than that. In fact, there has to be more to it than that.
The voice of vibration and its incessant mockery of this poor girl is just what we can bear witness to.
Who knows what must lurk inside of her? Who knows what it is that we can’t see?
And who knows how close I may have come to grazing it with the tips of my fingers during my new and exciting venture into her most private depths.
If I could pull it out, I would.
If I could reach all the way to her heart and swipe away the fog with a quick flick of the wrist, she wouldn’t need to rely on someone else who’s broken to try and fix her.
That sort of thing will never work.
Ah.
There’s the irony.
: Do you need to go to the nurse’s office? Do you want us to call Maki?
: Do you need anything? Can you even hear me right now?
scene mikupoolscene2
: What the heck? Where did this even come from? She was fine earlier.
: Should I go get Makoto? She should still be in the class or Sensei’s office or something. Maybe she’ll know what to do?
: You can try. But if it really is fatigue, I don’t think there’s anything we can do but let her rest. And the pool isn’t exactly the best place for that.
scene mikupoolscene3
: Sensei, I’m sorry to ask such a big favor of you- but would you mind bringing Miku to the nurse’s office? I’d do it myself, but I promised Miss Imai I’d take care of everything here in her absence.
: Sensei?...
That’s the wrong idea.
As the one person here who knows this isn’t just “fatigue,” taking Miku to the nurse’s office won’t do anything but make what’s likely wrong with her even more apparent.
And that will incriminate me. Or could incriminate me if either Miku or Io accidentally mention to someone that this is something I’ve known about.
But they wouldn’t do that, right? Even if they talk too much, they wouldn’t do that. They like me. And nobody else-
Makoto. Makoto would figure it out. She’d figure out that this is something I’ve been aware of. I’ve given her so many hints.
And it would not only ruin my relationship with her if this is serious, but open me up to further consequences as well if she made my involvement publicly known. Which she might.
Because even if she likes me, this is an area she won’t budge on. Even if she likes me, she likes Miku more. And she’ll know that I’ve been letting this happen.
Taking Miku to the nurse will ignite a spark that could burn down my entire life. I can’t have that. I can’t risk losing anything over taking her to the wrong place.

I should take her somewhere quieter. Safer. But not so quiet and safe that no one would ever find her. Besides, she’ll be okay. Right? She probably just took too much of something and needs to come down.
Everything will be fine. I should hide this. If I hide it, I can talk to her when she’s more conscious and make her stop.
There’s no need to risk destroying anything over this. I can just take her somewhere else. It’s that easy. I’m such a genius.
: What if I just took her back to the dorm?
scene mikupoolscene4
: The dorm? But that’s like a mile away. And I highly doubt Miku will be able to walk in this condition if she’s not even waking up for me.
: Then I’ll carry her. It’s fine.
: You’re going to...carry her all the way back there?
: It’s fine. Look at her. She can’t weigh any more than like 80lbs max.
: I mean...you’re the teacher. And I know better than to talk back if you think you know what’s best. So if that’s your decision, okay. But I’d appreciate if you’d text me when you get to her room.
: Just let me take her back to the locker room and change her clothes before-
: I’ll just carry her like that. Stripping a girl while she’s unconscious isn’t really a thing we’re supposed to do.
: Besides, putting her normal clothes back on might overheat her. She needs to get some rest as soon as possible. She can get dressed when she wakes back up.
scene mikupoolscene5
: A...Again...if that’s what you think is best...
: It is. I’ve thought a lot about this.
: Come on, Miku. We’re going now.
scene black
I make my way over to Miku and lift her off of the bench.
It’s clear that Karin is worried about what’s going on here and what I’ve decided to do, but that worry will only be temporary.
Once Miku goes back to normal and regains control of her limbs, this will all fade and there will never be anything to worry about again.
She’ll be good as new in no time at all. And it’ll all be because of me and how I avoided revealing to everyone that she’s casually overdosing on medication that wasn’t prescribed to her.
You’re welcome, Miku. And Io. And everyone else that I am saving and/or protecting by deciding to do this.
This is the right choice. I am making the right choice.
scene mikupoolscene6
I am making the right choice.
And if anything happens to her, it won’t be my fault.
Except it will.
But it won’t.
It will be Io’s fault.
I told her to stop this.
I did my part.
And there’s nothing I could have done to avoid this.
Which is why I will fix it now.
Which is why I will take her home.
And it is there she will recover and we’ll laugh all about this the next time we talk.
I am making the right choice.
: Sensei?...Is she a little heavy after all? If you really need help, I can-
scene mikupoolscene7
: No. I’m fine. I’m making the right choice.
: I...I trust your judgement. But again, please let me know as soon as-
scene black
: Come on, Miku. It’s time to go home.
: As soon as...
: ...you get to her room.
scene noonsky
This isn’t so bad.
She really is light.
And she doesn’t even smell like chlorine since she never made it into the pool today.
All things considered, this could have gone a lot worse.
People could be looking at me.
But no one seems to care that I’m carrying a partially conscious teenage girl wearing nothing but skintight latex to GOD knows where in broad daylight.
This is a totally normal thing and I’m totally normal for doing it and Miku is going to be totally fine and it’ll be totally awesome.
scene mikupoolscene8
Oh, okay. I guess we’re here now. That’s good. I saved the day.
I wonder when her eyes closed.

She’s still breathing. I can see the air exiting and entering her body. Just not the literal air. What I mean is that her body is moving. But only the part that air goes into. Which I guess also isn’t accurate but-

Anyway, we’re here. I did my job. Time to put Miku into her bed and then leave because what she needs is rest and not medical attention. You know what they say about time being the best medicine and all.
scene mikupoolscene9
Okay. She’s in bed now. Job done.
But is it okay if she stays like this? Should I take her clothes off? Is she too hot? Is she too cold? Does she need another blanket or no blanket at all?
Wait. There was something else I was supposed to do, wasn’t there?
I have to call someone.
But who-
Nevermind. I remember.
They answer.
: Hello?
Fuck. No. Not her. Someone else.
Uhh...
Screw it. They’ll contact me if it’s really that important and I can just say I don’t remember anything.

A sound slithers through the slight gap in Miku’s lips then grows legs, sprints across the mattress, and throws a grappling hook over my shoulder before climbing up and entering me through my left nostril.
A small man that was living inside of Miku spends the rest of his life building a home inside of my cranium and we all live happily ever after. Isn’t symbolism just the coolest?
scene mikupoolscene10
Just like I said — I did my job and now everything is good.
I have saved Miku’s life and prevented all of us from suffering or losing a valuable member of the class in one fell swoop.
Ami would be so proud of me if she could see me right now.
But I’ll call her again just to make sure.
Here she is.
scene mikupoolscene11
: Hey! What’s going on? I kinda figured the first call was just an accident since you hung up right away. Do you actually need something?
: No. I just wanted to tell you I did a good job today.
: You...do a good job every day, Sensei. Did something happen, though?
: No. Nothing happened except for the good deed I did.
: Where are you?
: Everywhere and nowhere, all at once.
: Do you need me to come get you?
I hang up the phone because Ami doesn’t understand and redirect my attention to Miku, whose eyes are now open because I did a thing.
: Sensei?...
: That’s my name. Just it isn’t. My real name is Akira. Hello.
: Wass...goin’ on?...
: Feel like I was just at school a minute ago...How’d I get here?...
: I carried you here because I’m awesome and responsible and was protecting you from the nurse so we can keep spending time together in the future and I don’t have to leave.
: You carried me here...all the way from school?...Why?...
: Because you’re a fucking idiot and have been taking random pills that Io gives you for an indeterminate amount of time now.
: But I didn’t even take any of those today...
: What?...
scene mikupoolscene12
: Or maybe I did...I don’t remember...
: Well, you’re not anymore. You’re done. No more medication without seeing a doctor first.
: Io says doctors are the worst...
: Io says everyone is the worst.
: Not me...Io likes me...
: No, Io likes playing pharmacist — which you go along with because you have the IQ of a rhinoceros beetle and don’t understand the potential consequences of your actions.
: Maybe...you’re the one who doesn’t understand?...
: That’s exactly what she told me. But you’re both wrong. How much did you take today?
: I already told you, I don’t remember. But I won’t take that much again. Promise.
: You can’t keep that promise if you don’t even know how much it was, Miku.
: Heheh...you got me...
: Thanks for carryin’ me, though...That was real nice of ya...
: The alternative was taking you to someone who would have understood what was happening and it would have spiraled into something horrible.
: How come understanding what’s happening has to be bad?...
: That part isn’t bad. The bad part is how I wouldn’t have been able to keep my mouth shut and how Io could get in trouble for it and how Makoto would stop having sex with me.
: That’s fine...You can just have sex with me instead...
: I probably don’t know the same sex moves as her, though...
: Come on...
: What’re ya waitin’ for?...
: Do it already...
: That was your invitation, Sensei...
: Ya gonna make me spell it out?...
: Miku...are you out of your mind?
scene mikupoolscene13
: Yeah.
: I kinda am.
: That’s kinda why I started seein’ Dr. Io in the first place. And it’s been workin’ out real well.
: Just look how long my hair’s gettin’. I ain’t pulled any out in months. And I ain’t scared of anything anymore.
: Worst thing that’s happened is you havin’ to carry me home. But even that ain’t bad since ya get to stick it in me now.
: Absolutely not.
: Really? Is that thing about boys wantin’ sex all the time just a rumor after all? I fall for those pretty easily, so it wouldn’t be weird if I was wrong.
: I’m not going to have sex with someone coming down from a minor overdose.
: How long do we gotta wait? Cause I can’t really feel anythin’ right now and figured this would be a good chance to give you my v-card without gettin’ hurt.
: If you’re okay, I’m going to leave now.
: Without even fingering me? But we’re all alone. Ya gotta give me somethin’ here.
: I don’t have to give you anything. And, to be honest, I kind of don’t even want to look at you right now.
scene mikupoolscene14
: You...bein’ serious?...
: I can’t really tell...
: I am. This isn’t like you, Miku. You’re not the type of person to do things like this.
: S’cuse me for puttin’ it bluntly, but...the heck do you know about who I really am?
: You ain’t got the first idea of what I’m dealin’ with. You don’t get it at all, Sensei.
: It’s hard to get something when you’d rather knock yourself out than open up to me.
: You’re the same friggin’ way.
: I don’t know anythin’ about you and I still squeeze the cum outta ya because I’m a good friend and we don’t need to know that kinda stuff about each other.
: And that’s fair. But your way of avoiding difficult confrontation is slowly killing you.
scene mikupoolscene15
: So is yours...only difference is that ain’t nobody strong enough to carry you home...
: That’s not the same thing, Miku. This is-
: Listen, Sensei — my head is kinda poundin’ and my throat is really dry, so if you’re not gonna stick your wiener in me, could ya maybe let me take a nap or somethin’? Thanks.
: I don’t like this side of you, Miku. This isn’t the person I know.
: Cry me a friggin’ river. Night, Sensei.
scene black
There will be no river, nor tears at all-
For it hurts the most before the fall.
Then afterwards, with broken bones-
And flesh untucked from dermal homes-
The sky is where we find salvation.
Our final sight and last sensation.
As eyes roll back, and respiration-
Contorts our lungs in expiration-
We’ll rely on half-unpacked narration
And take shelter in these new vibrations.
This one was me.
But I wish that it wasn’t.
So I’ll forget it immediately.
There is no narrator I can ever rely on.
Everyone just wants to break me.
But no one can finish the job.

$ mikublock = True
$ miku_love += 1
Miku’s affection has increased to [miku_love] for the remainder of the night, but it goes back down the morning after when she has trouble remembering what happened.
You hurt yourself when you got home, but only you will know what that means.
